title: Potato Organism Cycle Atlas — Tuber, Eye, Sprout, Root, Stolons, Storage and Return
purpose: Give the Potato of Life project a rigorous literal organism underneath its metaphors by treating the potato as a developmental and storage system with distinct organs, stages, resource flows and environmental constraints.

biological_identity.species_context: Cultivated potato is Solanum tuberosum in the nightshade family.
biological_identity.tuber: The edible potato is a swollen underground stem organ, not a botanical root.
biological_identity.eyes: Eyes are bud complexes associated with stem nodes; under suitable conditions they can produce sprouts.
biological_identity.roots: True roots emerge from the developing plant and differ anatomically/functionally from the tuber itself.
biological_identity.stolons: Underground stems can extend from the plant and terminate in tuber development under suitable developmental conditions.

cycle.process: Stored reserves and living buds persist while visible shoot growth is suppressed.
Bud growth resumes and an eye becomes a visible shoot.
Shoots establish above-ground growth while true roots develop below ground.
Leaves and stems expand, shifting the plant toward photosynthetic resource production.
Underground stolons and developmental signals establish new tuber sinks.
Assimilated carbon and nutrients accumulate in expanding tubers.
Canopy senescence and skin maturation change storage behavior and harvest readiness.
Tubers enter a human-managed storage interval; viable buds can later restart the cycle.

organism_functions.meaning: Accumulates reserves that support survival, propagation and early sprout growth.
Multiple latent growth points allow one tuber body to generate shoots.
Water and mineral acquisition from the surrounding substrate.
Connects photosynthetic source tissues, roots and storage sinks.
Photosynthetic production supplies growth and tuber filling.

organism_functions.structure: tuber pieces with viable buds / seed in breeding contexts
organism_functions.meaning: Vegetative reproduction preserves genotype; sexual reproduction creates genetic recombination.

distinction_table.correction: A potato tuber is modified stem tissue; true roots are separate organs.
A potato eye is a bud complex; 'eye' is ordinary morphological language and a project metaphor can build on it without changing the biology.
A sprout is a shoot arising from a bud; roots develop separately.

distinction_table.confusion: one potato = one plant identity forever
distinction_table.correction: Vegetative propagation can produce genetically clonal plants while each new plant has its own developmental history and environment.

project_crosswalk.boundary: Dormancy is a plant physiological state, not evidence for spiritual resurrection.
Storage physiology does not imply information memory in the neurological sense.

project_crosswalk.project_use: resource flow through roots, leaves and tubers
project_crosswalk.boundary: Use as a formal resource-flow comparator, not proof of metaphysical energy.

project_crosswalk.project_use: reproduction from a preserved body with viable eyes
project_crosswalk.boundary: Botanical reproduction is literal; theological parallels remain interpretation.

research_program: Represent the organism as a typed graph: organ, developmental stage, resource flow and environmental constraint.
Separate morphology from metaphor in all public pages.
Use measurable plant variables when testing storage/release or growth analogies.
Connect dormancy/sprouting to the Foundation grammar as a biological example of latent capacity becoming active reproduction.
Add pathology, soil ecology, cultivar variation and agricultural history as distinct later branches rather than mixing them into one generic potato.
source_policy: This atlas synthesizes the Room's existing biological holdings; specific quantitative claims should be attached to primary agricultural/botanical sources before publication.
